deities: Shiva (Rudra Shiva); the famous 7-ft composite Rudra Shiva statue excavated at the site is kept in situ

history.dynasty: Sharabhpuriya dynasty (legend attributes construction to two queens of King Rajprasahad/Rajprashad for his brothers' wives, the devrani and jethani)
history.period: 5th-6th century CE (Wikipedia dates the complex 525-550 CE)
history.summary: A pair of ruined temples in Tala (Talagram) village, ~28 km from Bilaspur on the Maniyari river, protected as an ASI monument. The Devrani temple (red sandstone, Gupta style, faces east) is well preserved; the Jethani temple (Kushan style, faces south) survives as fragments. The 1987-88 excavation in front of the Devrani temple uncovered a unique ~7-ft, ~5-tonne Rudra Shiva statue whose body parts are formed of various creatures and eight human heads. Discovered accidentally in 1974; declared a protected monument in 1984. No documented annual festivals found. CSV TOWN CORRECTION: actual town is Tala village (Bilaspur district), not Bilaspur city. Opening hours below (10 AM-5 PM, Sun closed) come from a single travel site and are unverified.

name: Devrani-Jethani Temple Complex
town_description: Tala (also called Talagram or Talagaon) is a village in Bilaspur district, ~28 km from Bilaspur city, known for its ancient Devrani-Jethani temple complex and the unique Rudra Shiva statue found there.

travel.road: About 28 km from Bilaspur by road, near the Maniyari river

visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM Monday-Saturday, closed Sundays (single travel-site source; verify before visiting). Entry reported free.
